subject: biology
title: Antibiotics and painkillers
key_idea: Antibiotics kill bacteria inside the body but do not kill viruses. Painkillers only treat symptoms and do not kill pathogens. Overusing antibiotics leads to resistant bacteria, so doctors prescribe them carefully.

blocks.text: Antibiotics are medicines used to cure bacterial disease. This section covers how they work and why they do not work against viruses.

items.meaning: A chemical, usually made by fungi or microbes, that kills bacteria inside the body.
When bacteria are no longer killed by an antibiotic.

items: Antibiotics, such as **penicillin**, cure bacterial disease by killing the bacteria inside the body.
They inhibit processes in the bacteria, for example by disrupting cell walls, so the bacteria are killed or stop reproducing.
They do not damage the body's own (host) cells.
Specific bacteria must be treated with specific antibiotics.
Antibiotics do not kill **viruses**. Viruses live inside cells, and it is difficult to make drugs that kill viruses without also damaging the body's tissues.
Antibiotics kill bacteria. They do not work on viruses.
Each type of bacterium needs the correct antibiotic.
Antibiotics have greatly reduced deaths from bacterial diseases.

blocks.text: Not every medicine kills a pathogen. This section compares the other types that you need to know.

diagram.alt: Sort each statement into the type of medicine it describes: antibiotic, painkiller or antiseptic.
diagram.prompt: Which type of medicine does each statement describe?

items.text: Treats the symptoms of a disease
Wiped on the skin before surgery to kill bacteria
Used on living tissue, not taken inside the body

items: **Painkillers** and other medicines treat the symptoms of disease. They do not kill pathogens.
**Antivirals** are used to treat viral infections, for example hepatitis. Antibiotics would not be given.
Antiseptics are used outside the body, for example on the skin before surgery, to kill bacteria.
Painkillers treat symptoms. They do not cure the disease.
A viral infection is treated with an antiviral, not an antibiotic.
Antibiotics are used inside the body. Antiseptics are not.

blocks.text: New strains of bacteria have become resistant to antibiotics. This is of great concern to doctors.

items: Current antibiotics do not kill resistant bacteria.
Some diseases become more difficult to treat, and new antibiotics take time and money to develop.
Doctors do not prescribe antibiotics for viral infections or mild infections, which the body's immune system can deal with.
Patients must finish the course. Any bacteria left may develop resistance, survive and reproduce.
A resistant strain is only treated with the antibiotic that kills it, so routine use is avoided.
Hospitals use hand wash and disinfectant, and isolate patients with the resistant strain.
Resistant bacteria survive antibiotics and reproduce.
Antibiotics should only be prescribed for bacterial infections that need them.
Finish the whole course.

checks.q: Explain why antibiotics cannot be used to treat a viral disease.
checks.a: Antibiotics only kill bacteria. They do not destroy viruses, which live inside cells.

checks.q: Give one reason why a patient with a cold caused by a virus should not be given antibiotics.
checks.a: Antibiotics do not kill viruses, and using them unnecessarily helps antibiotic-resistant bacteria to spread.

checks.q: State what painkillers do in the treatment of disease.
checks.a: They treat the symptoms of the disease but do not kill the pathogens.

exam_phrases: do not prescribe antibiotics for viral infections
because antibiotics do not kill viruses
make sure the patient finishes the course
any bacteria left may develop resistance, survive and reproduce
current / available antibiotics do not kill (certain) bacteria
some diseases become more difficult to treat

mistakes.wrong: Doctors are concerned because more people become ill.
mistakes.right: This is ignored. Say that current antibiotics do not kill certain bacteria, so some diseases become more difficult to cure or treat.

mistakes.wrong: Antibiotics should not be used for colds because the bacteria get used to them.
mistakes.right: Colds and flu are caused by viruses, and antibiotics do not kill viruses. Resistance happens when bacteria that survive reproduce.

mistakes.wrong: Clean the hospital to remove bacteria.
mistakes.right: Be specific: use antibacterial or alcohol hand wash between patients, use disinfectant on wards, and isolate patients with the resistant strain.

worked_example.question:
Pseudomonas bacteria cause infections in hospital patients. A new strain of Pseudomonas bacteria has evolved. This new strain can only be killed by one antibiotic called fluroquinolone. Scientists want to prevent the new strain of Pseudomonas from spreading in the human population.

Explain the advice doctors should be given to prevent the spread of the new strain.
answer_points: Do not prescribe fluroquinolone or antibiotics for mild infections, because they will get better due to the body's normal immune system.
Do not prescribe antibiotics for viral infections such as colds or flu, because antibiotics do not kill viruses.
If antibiotics are prescribed, make sure the patient finishes the course, because any bacteria left may develop resistance, survive and reproduce.
Only prescribe fluroquinolone if the patient has the new strain, because routine use would lead to an increase in resistant bacteria.
Use antibacterial or alcohol hand wash between each patient and disinfectant to clean wards, to kill resistant bacteria.
Isolate patients with this strain, to prevent other patients getting the resistant infection.
worked_example.tip: This is a levelled question. Give advice and a linked reason for each point to reach the top level.

exam_phrases: so bacteria are destroyed / are killed / growth stops / reproduction stops
antibiotics do not affect the host cell
it is killed / inhibited by antibiotics
because chlamydia is caused by bacteria

mistakes.right: "Inhibit the bacteria" or "inhibit cell processes" on its own is ignored. Say that antibiotics inhibit processes in the bacteria so they are killed or stop growing or reproducing.
Antibiotics only treat bacterial infections. Chlamydia can be treated because it is caused by bacteria.

mistakes.wrong: Antibiotics work by killing any cell they meet.
mistakes.right: Antibiotics do not affect or damage the host (human) cells, which is why they can be used inside the body.

worked_example.question:
Some bacteria are pathogens.

Explain why antibiotics can be used to treat bacterial infections.
answer_points: They inhibit processes in the bacteria.
So the bacteria are destroyed or killed (growth or reproduction stops).
But antibiotics do not affect or damage the host cell.
worked_example.tip: Any two of these points score. Named processes, such as disrupting cell walls, are accepted.

exam_phrases: a chemical (usually) made by fungi / microbes
would not give antibiotics / (would give) an antiviral
wants to avoid the spread of antibiotic resistant (bacteria)

mistakes.wrong: Doctors do not give antibiotics for a virus because the virus can become antibiotic resistant.
mistakes.right: Viruses do not become antibiotic resistant. Bacteria do. Say antibiotics do not kill viruses and that doctors want to avoid the spread of resistant bacteria.

mistakes.wrong: The doctor would give a vaccine to treat a viral disease.
mistakes.right: A vaccine is ignored. Say the doctor would give an antiviral, not an antibiotic.

mistakes.wrong: Antiseptics are taken inside the body like antibiotics.
mistakes.right: Antibiotics are used inside the body, but antiseptics are not.

worked_example.question:
A patient in hospital has a bacterial disease. The doctor gives the patient a tablet containing a medicine that will kill the bacteria.

The doctor would change the type of medicine given to the patient if the disease was caused by a virus.

State the change the doctor would make. Give a reason for your answer.
answer_points: Change: the doctor would not give antibiotics, and would give an antiviral.
Reason: viruses are not destroyed by antibiotics (antibiotics only kill bacteria).
worked_example.tip: One mark for the change and one for the reason. Mentioning a vaccine is ignored.
